title: Monotonicity in function values
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and $p>0$. For functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, suppose $f$ is nonnegative and $f(x)\le g(x)$ for every $x$. Then $M_p(f)\le M_p(g)$, where $M_p$ is the extended power mean under the uniform measure.
replaced: For $p>0$ and functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ satisfying $0\le f(x)\le g(x)$ for every $x$, one has $M_p(f)\le M_p(g)$, where $M_p(u)=(\E|u|^p)^{1/p}$.
